elements.texte:
[cheerful] Normalizing a database means organizing its information into several tables linked together.

This limits repetition and avoids errors when changes are made.

The customers table already exists.

So we add three tables.

The workshops and coaches tables contain the sessions on offer and who leads them.

The enrollments table records who takes part in which workshop.

Your turn!

The title and date describe the workshop; the name and email describe the coach.

The enrollment date describes the link between a customer and a workshop: it goes in the enrollments table.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] This organization follows three rules, applied in order: the normal forms.

1st normal form: each cell holds only one value.

So two workshops never go in the same cell: each enrollment has its own row.

2nd normal form: each column depends on the whole key.

An enrollment is identified by the customer and the workshop: the enrollment date depends on both.

The workshop date depends only on the workshop: it goes in the workshops table.

3rd normal form: no column depends on a column other than the key.

The email depends on the coach, not on the workshop: it goes in the coaches table.
